# Reference launcher comparison: upstream fork vs this branch

**Reference:** `funnymataleao/luma-webos-launcher` @ `40994fc144b5af481056d14e2fb93304aa1e2c82` (tree `ff2314ecd0cc8955874447784005a1c430f4cebc`, `src` tree `f7425e26ba76a94dbf07a06c8927778d375ec90f`, tag `v2.2.160`, MIT).
**Ours:** `SteveSpivak/lg-luma` @ base `e5608cd053be5376a54a806129a332952dfabcef` (Luma 2.16.2, `com.ecklf.luma`), candidate patch `8230cce6…` still **unapplied**.
**Facts:** `research/audit/reference-launcher-facts.json` (generated by `research/scripts/compare_reference_launcher.py`, pinned-clone only, never imported into this checkout).

## Verdict

This is not a newer version of our tree. It is a **sibling fork of `ecklf/lg-luma`** with a nearly disjoint feature set: they invested in media/connectivity surfaces and a motion design system; we invested in damage-tracked rendering, self-update, tooling and evidence discipline. 126 blobs are byte-identical, 53 shared files diverged, and neither tree contains the other's distinctive modules.

On the one axis where the work actually overlaps — **focus depth** — their change is a design system (continuous level, spring, zoom, wide halo, reduced-motion gates) and ours is a single parameter swap behind an exact-match environment variable. Their focused card costs ~2.6× the shadow area of my candidate and adds a 7 % zoom; my candidate adds **12.49 %** shadow area to the focused card and nothing else. That makes my patch the smaller, cheaper, more reversible experiment, but also the less ambitious one, and it does not reproduce their perceived depth, which comes mostly from the halo and zoom rather than the shadow.

Nothing here was measured on a GPU, a TV or a wall clock. Every number below is `OBSERVED` (git/source), `MODEL` (closed-form arithmetic from source constants) or `NOT_RUN`.

Both trees descend from the same upstream, which is why `vector-geometry/*` (2/2), `.changeset/*` (2/2), `license`, `.gitignore`, `flake.lock`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and 103 `assets/` blobs are byte-identical. Their history is a squashed import, so **no incremental design rationale is recoverable from commits** — only from `development.md`.

Because the app id differs, their build installs as a *separate application*; it cannot silently replace `com.ecklf.luma`. That matters for our "do not modify Home hooks / TV configuration" constraint: the reference's Home-takeover and root features are opt-in on a rooted TV and are outside our approval regardless.

`jellyfin`, `plex`, `moonlight`, `player` + `player_backend` + `player_view` + `media`, `library`/`movie`/`album`/`music`/`game` views, `steam`, `stacks`, `smart_home` (+`_pairing`, `_settings_view`, `_ws`), `widgets` (+`_settings_view`, `_state`, `_view`), `phone_link`, `mini`, `pad_watch`, `typography`, `settings_art`, `motion`, `weather_sky`, `hw_wallpaper`, `aerial_video`, plus `native/smp/*` (C/C++ façade over `StarfishMediaAPIs`) and `native/cinema/*`.

### Shared modules grew on their side

Shared code is 25,594 reference lines vs 19,830 ours (−22.5 %): `state.rs` +2,654, `main.rs` +2,173, `view.rs` +1,143, `renderer.rs` +1,043. Their fork carried the core forward with the feature work; ours kept the core smaller and added orthogonal modules.

## 3. Focus and elevation: their system vs my patch

### Theirs

- Focus is continuous: `focus_level()` returns a tween value with `FOCUS_IN = FOCUS_OUT = 0.16 s`, or a hard 0/1 under `preferences.reduced_motion` (`src/state.rs:999`).
- `focus_pop()` is a designed overshoot curve `1 − e^(−5k)·cos(10k)` over `FOCUS_POP = 0.55 s`, plus a one-shot "sheen" sweep of `FOCUS_SHEEN = 0.4` (`src/state.rs:1010`).
- Apps cards zoom `1 + 0.07 · pop` and draw a *layered* shadow: `26 + 14·level` blur, `8 + 4·level` offset, `0.14 + 0.1·level` alpha, then an `accent_glow` halo of `blur 90`, offset 16, alpha `0.3·level` on a rect inset by 8 (`src/view.rs:1338`, `src/view.rs:383`).
- Perf trade-off baked into the view: on the Apps page, resting cards **skip their shadow entirely** (`if state.page != Page::Apps || level > 0.`), justified in a comment as keeping the focus sheen smooth.
- 48 `out.shadow(...)` call sites across 10 files; 28 pass interpolated expressions. 123 `reduced_motion` references gate the motion.

### Mine

One Apps-card shadow parameter set, gated by exact `LUMA_FOCUS_DEPTH=1`: focused `blur 34→42`, `dy 14→20`, `alpha 0.4→0.5`; unfocused stays `22/9/0.165`. No zoom, no halo, no sheen, no timer, no persistent setting, no state change.

### Parameter comparison (OBSERVED constants, derived ratios MODEL)

| Metric | Ours (current) | Ours (experiment) | Reference (focused) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Shadow blur | 34 | 42 | 40 + 90 halo |
| Vertical offset | 14 | 20 | 12 (halo 16) |
| Alpha | 0.40 | 0.50 | 0.24 (halo 0.30 → composite 0.468) |
| Depth index `dy / 154.4` | 0.0907 | 0.1295 | 0.0777 |
| Softness `blur / 154.4` | 0.2202 | 0.2720 | 0.2591 (halo 0.5829) |
| Contrast `blur / dy` | 2.43 | 2.10 | 3.33 (halo 5.63) |
| Zoom | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0864 at spring peak |
| Shadow quad area | 72,057.6 px² | 81,056 px² | 212,486.4 px² |

Reading these dimensionless numbers: their focused card is **softer and closer to the surface** (low depth index, high blur/dy) plus a halo — the "floating" cue. Mine is **darker and farther** (higher depth index, lower blur/dy) — a heavier, cast-shadow cue. They are not the same look, and mine is not a cheap imitation of theirs; it is a different, single-variable hypothesis.

## 4. Speed model (MODEL — no GPU or TV measurement)

Shadow draws are alpha-blended SDF quads expanded by `blur` (`src/renderer.rs:1255`, `paint.frag`), so fill grows as `(w + 2b)(h + 2b)`; damage uses `blur + 1` (`src/damage.rs:88`).

| Measure | Ours current | Ours experiment | Ref (Home) | Ref (Apps) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Grid fill, 14 resting + 1 focused (px) | 905,337.6 | 914,336.0 | 1,102,483.2 | 212,486.4 |
| Share of a 1080p frame | 43.66 % | 44.09 % | 53.17 % | 10.25 % |
| Shadow bytes/frame (RGBA8) | 3.62 MB | 3.66 MB | 4.41 MB | 0.85 MB |
| Implied traffic at 60 Hz (read+write) | 0.435 GB/s | 0.439 GB/s | 0.529 GB/s | 0.102 GB/s |
| Focused-card damage | 73,154.4 px² | 82,216.8 px² | — | — |

For scale: one full 1080p RGBA8 frame is 8,294,400 B, i.e. 0.4977 GB/s at 60 Hz; a 4K buffer is 33,177,600 B and a double buffer 66,355,200 B.

What this says:

1. **My patch is a rounding error next to the frame budget**: +8,998.4 px² (+12.49 %) on one card, +9,062.4 px² of damage, about **+0.4 %** of a full-screen pass. If this alone visibly changes pacing, the bottleneck is not shadow fill.
2. **The shadow pass is not free in aggregate**: on a 15-card grid it is already ~44 % of a full-screen composite on our side and ~53 % on theirs. That is the real argument for a budgeted shadow, not the focused card.
3. **Their Apps optimisation is the biggest single lever in either tree** (−43 % of frame fill on that page) but it pays with a visual: resting cards lose their shadow entirely. It is a benchmark-free trade, exactly the kind of change our constraints say must be measured before it ships.
4. Their halo is large — 133,728 px², **3.38×** the card face — which is why their Home grid costs more than ours despite skipping shadows on Apps.

## 5. Motion math and physics

- **Spring is not a physical solution.** `1 − e^(−5k)·cos(10k)` has no sine term, so it is not the step response of a damped oscillator; the envelope and the oscillation were chosen independently. Its first turning point is at `k = (π − atan(0.5))/10 = 0.2678` (`t = 147 ms`), peak `1.23444`, overshoot **23.44 %**, settling to ±1 % at `0.5066 s` within the 0.55 s budget.
- **Equivalent damping** for a true second-order system with that overshoot is `ζ = 0.4192` — plausible for UI, but call it "equivalent", not "the system's damping".
- **Zoom**: `1 + 0.07 · pop` peaks at `1.08641`, i.e. **+18.03 %** area for the focused card; scaling is about the centre, so neighbouring cards are occluded rather than reflowed.
- **Chase** (their scroll follower): `λ = 3.22/0.18 = 17.889 s⁻¹`, `τ = 55.9 ms`, 96 % in `179.9 ms` (≈10.8 frames at 60 Hz), 99 % in `257.4 ms`, with a 0.35 deadband snap. The code comment ("96 % in ~180 ms") checks out exactly.
- **Penumbra is linear-in-distance, not optical**: alpha is `1 − smoothstep(−blur, blur, d)` over a signed-distance field. There is no Gaussian kernel, no contact hardening, no physically based light. "Softness" here is literally the band width; the blur parameter is not a physical penumbra in metres.
- **Composite alpha** of their two stacked shadows is `1 − (1−0.24)(1−0.30) = 0.468`, close to my single `0.5` — so near-contact darkness is comparable even though the falloff is not.

## 6. Documentation: claims vs code

| Claim (reference docs) | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Glyph geometry 8 MiB / 4096 entries | `GLYPH_GEOMETRY_BUDGET = 8 MiB`, `glyphs.len() > 4096` (`renderer.rs:116,616`) | **VERIFIED** |
| Text runs 32 MiB / 512 entries | `TEXT_GEOMETRY_BUDGET = 32 MiB`, `text_runs.len() > 512` (`renderer.rs:117,635`) | **VERIFIED** |
| Raster artwork 48 MiB budget | `CACHE_BYTES = 48 MiB` (`app_artwork.rs:25`) | **VERIFIED** |
| "Idle screens draw on demand; VSync paces animation" | `diagnostics.rs` doc comment; `Profile::pause()` | **VERIFIED (source)** |
| Pacing ≠ GPU time | `cpu_submission` recorded separately; comment says so explicitly | **VERIFIED (source)** |
| 4K native presentation | `development.md`: C5/O22A3/lg1kdrm test table, corruption, explicit "does not prove 1:1 presentation" | **THIRD-PARTY PHYSICAL EVIDENCE**, not ours; not reusable as a claim |
| "Stays smooth on TV hardware" (README) | no numbers, no methodology | **UNVERIFIED** |
| "Every change was checked on the TV before release" | maintainer statement, 5-commit import | **DECLARED**, not independently verifiable |

Their `development.md` is the strongest document in either tree: it states limits ("a 4K screenshot or drawable alone does not prove 1:1 panel presentation") that match the standard we hold ourselves to. Their README's smoothness claim does not meet that same bar.

## 7. Forensics and hygiene (OBSERVED)

- **No embedded credentials**: zero matches for private-key blocks, AWS keys, GitHub/Slack tokens, literal JWTs or assigned passwords across `src`, `tools`, `tests`, `native`, `tv`, `extras`. `ApiKey=` appears only inside Jellyfin URL templates and one settings label.
- **No DRM code**: zero matches for Widevine, PlayReady, HDCP or "drm". 52 `netflix` mentions are app-id/branding strings, not stream handling.
- **LG headers are included, not vendored**: `#include <NDL_directmedia.h>` (1 site) resolves against the on-device SDK; no `NDL_*.h` is redistributed. `native/smp/vendor/smp_api.h` is their own C façade over `StarfishMediaAPIs` and documents per-webOS-generation ABI differences.
- **Assets are licensed**: 36 `OFL.txt` files next to 36 bundled TTFs (43.0 MB); 607 JPEGs (84.1 MB) and 121 SVGs; total 137.5 MB vendored. Under our standing constraint these are **not importable** — the licenses permit it, our instructions do not.
- **Supply-chain surface**: 5 commits, unsigned, `pnpm-lock.yaml` 93,780 B, `Cargo.lock` 51,315 B, one CI workflow. Their CI (`ci.yml:41–93`) is the reference for real desktop validation: apt `libsdl2-dev pkg-config woff2 python3-fonttools libgl1-mesa-dri xvfb xauth`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`, `xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1920x1080x24' pnpm test:smoke`, then uploads `.build/*.png` and `.build/*-render.json`.
- **No secret exfiltration surface found** in the reviewed text; network calls are Open-Meteo, media servers, Home Assistant and public exchange APIs per the README.

## 8. Where each architecture wins

| Concern | Reference | Ours | Better |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle/partial redraw | draw-on-demand; whole-scene recompose per focus frame | `damage.rs` + `egl_damage.rs` region tracking | **Ours** (structural) |
| Measuring redraw cost | aggregate mean/p95/max pacing | per-frame `timeline` with `compose/render/swap/redrawn/glyph/vector/image` | **Ours** (superset: 17 serialized fields vs 8) |
| Shadow overdraw | skip resting shadows on Apps; per-view constants | one global card shadow, no per-surface budget | **Theirs** (explicit budget) |
| Focus motion | level + spring + sheen + zoom + halo, 123 reduced-motion gates | none | **Theirs** (design), ours trivially safe |
| Content features | Jellyfin/Plex/Moonlight/HA/widgets/player | none of these | **Theirs** |
| Maintenance | self-update, install helper, tile editor, wallpapers, recents | present | **Ours** |
| Evidence discipline | budgets verified, 4K caveats, device table | runbook + BLOCKED gates + receipts | **Tie** |

Important nuance: our damage tracking avoids *redrawing unchanged content*, but during a focus sheen nearly every card changes, so it does not by itself remove the shadow cost their Apps hack targets. Claiming otherwise would be wrong.

## 9. Adopt / defer / reject

**Adopt (behaviour, not code):**
1. Continuous focus level with an explicit reduced-motion short-circuit — as a *design*, not as my candidate. My patch deliberately avoids motion so the A/B isolates depth.
2. The verified cache budgets as invariants: 8 MiB/4096 glyphs, 32 MiB/512 runs, 48 MiB raster. We already have the same constants; add doc-vs-code assertions instead of trusting prose.
3. Their CI smoke recipe as the concrete unblock for our Gate 3; it matches our `NATIVE-VALIDATION.md` dependency list (`xvfb xauth libsdl2-dev pkg-config woff2 python3-fonttools libgl1-mesa-dri`).
4. `.build/*-render.json` upload-diagnostics pattern: our analyzer already expects that schema.

**Defer (needs measurement we do not have):**
1. Per-surface shadow budget in the direction of theirs (large blur + halo). Cost is 2.6× my candidate; perceived gain unmeasured.
2. Dropping resting-card shadows on Apps. Biggest single fill cut in either tree, but it is a visible regression risk and must be A/B'd with our timeline.
3. Any zoom-on-focus: +18 % area, motion-dependent, needs a 60 Hz trace on target hardware.

**Reject:**
1. Importing their tree, assets, C helpers or vendored fonts (explicitly out of scope; also 137.5 MB of binaries).
2. Home takeover, root features, device-config changes.
3. Physical-TV claims derived from their `development.md` C5 table — it is third-party evidence about a different unit, not our measurement.

## 10. What this changes for my next step

The candidate stays exactly as it is: default-OFF, exact-match env var, static, 4 tests, reverse-apply proven. This comparison does **not** justify expanding it before the desktop baseline, and it does not justify importing any of their design.

What it does change:

1. **Add one measurable hypothesis, not a redesign.** After the OFF/ON desktop baseline, the defensible follow-up is a *shadow budget* test — the same env-gated parameter, with the grid-level fill (44 % of a frame at 15 cards) as the metric — instead of a halo/zoom system.
2. **Use their numbers as priors, not results.** 2.6× area for the halo is arithmetic on constants; whether it looks better is `NOT_RUN`.
3. **Our diagnostics are the prerequisite** for any of this: their aggregate summary could not attribute shadow cost, ours can.

## 11. Reproduce

```sh
# pinned reference, outside the checkout, blob-filtered
git clone --depth 1 --no-checkout --filter=blob:none \
  https://github.com/funnymataleao/luma-webos-launcher.git /home/user/luma-ref/luma-webos-launcher
cd /home/user/luma-ref/luma-webos-launcher
git sparse-checkout init --cone
git sparse-checkout set src native docs tools tests tv vector-geometry .github .changeset
git checkout   # HEAD must equal 40994fc144b5af481056d14e2fb93304aa1e2c82

cd /home/user/lg-luma
python3 -B research/scripts/compare_reference_launcher.py     # writes research/audit/reference-launcher-facts.json
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s research/tests -t research/tests -p 'test_reference_*.py'
```

## Evidence labels

`OBSERVED` — git object ids, file counts, source constants. `MODEL` — all pixel areas, area ratios, damage deltas, bandwidths, spring/chase timings; closed-form from constants, **not** a GPU, TV or wall-clock measurement. `NOT_RUN` — native build, OFF/ON rendering, visual difference, frame pacing, physical TV. `BLOCKED` — native toolchain absent (B01), full pnpm baseline (B02).
